title: Cubes, Dice & Cutting
relevance: Campus OAs and aptitude rounds routinely test painted-cube counting, die opposite-face deduction, and planar-cut minima as quick spatial-reasoning filters.

phases.goal: Establish painted-cube face-count formulas and the standard-die opposite-face rule.

must_hit.point: A solid cube painted on all sides and cut into n^3 identical smaller cubes always has exactly 8 corner cubes with 3 faces painted.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the 8 corners as the only 3-face-painted cubes, independent of n.

must_hit.point: With all faces painted: 2-face (edges) = 12(n-2), 1-face (face centres) = 6(n-2)^2, 0-face (inner core) = (n-2)^3; total smaller cubes = n^3.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites the four formulas and that they partition n^3.

must_hit.point: On a standard die, opposite faces always sum to 7 (e.g., 1 opposite 6).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States sum-to-7 and gives an opposite pair like 1 and 6.

probes: A cube is painted on all sides and cut into n^3 identical smaller cubes. How many have 3, 2, 1, or 0 faces painted?
On a standard die, what is opposite 3, and what rule are you using?

hints.1: Separate corners, edges, faces, and the hollowed-out interior.
hints.2: Corners are fixed; edges and faces shrink with (n-2); interior is a smaller cube of side (n-2).
hints.3: 8 corners; 12(n-2) edges; 6(n-2)^2 face centres; (n-2)^3 unpainted; standard die opposites sum to 7.

phases.goal: Apply counting formulas under edge cases and deduce die opposites from shared faces or cuts.

must_hit.point: Formulas using (n-2) for 1-face and 2-face painted cubes apply only when n >= 3; if n=2, (n-2)=0 so there are exactly 8 cubes with 3 painted faces and 0 with fewer.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flags the n>=3 precondition and the all-corners n=2 case.

must_hit.point: If two views of a die share exactly one face, write faces clockwise from that common face; corresponding terms in the two sequences are opposite each other.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes the one-common-face clockwise pairing rule.

must_hit.point: If two views share two faces, the remaining unmatched face in each view is opposite the other.
Without restacking, cutting into n×n×n identical pieces needs n-1 straight planar cuts along each of three perpendicular axes.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says n-1 cuts per axis, total 3(n-1).

probes: Why do the usual 1-face and 2-face painted counts break for a 2×2×2 dissection?
Two die views share exactly one face — how do you find which faces are opposite?
How many planar cuts (no restacking) turn a cube into 5×5×5 identical smaller cubes?

hints.1: Watch the (n-2) term, and for dice compare what is shared between views.
hints.2: n=2 is all corners; for one shared face use clockwise sequences; for cuts use n-1 per axis.
hints.3: n>=3 for (n-2) formulas; n=2 → 8 three-face only; one shared face → clockwise pairing; two shared → unmatched faces opposite; 125=5^3 needs 4+4+4=12 cuts.

phases.goal: Choose cut distributions to maximize pieces or minimize cuts, with and without restacking.

must_hit.point: With a fixed total of cuts x+y+z along three axes, pieces equal (x+1)(y+1)(z+1); maximize by keeping x, y, z as close as possible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States product form and even-split maximization (e.g., 10 cuts as 3,3,4 → 4×4×5=80).

must_hit.point: For a target of identical grid pieces x·y·z with no restacking, cuts equal x+y+z-3; minimize by choosing three factors of the target that are as close as possible.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives cuts = x+y+z-3 and close-factor minimization (e.g., 60=3×4×5 → 9 cuts).

must_hit.point: With restacking allowed, one cut can double the piece count; the theoretical minimum cuts to get N pieces is ceil(log2 N).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions doubling via restack and ceil(log2 N) (e.g., 64 pieces → 6 cuts).

probes: With exactly 10 straight cuts and no restacking, what is the maximum number of identical pieces you can get from a cube?
You need exactly 60 identical grid pieces with no restacking — how do you minimize cuts?
Minimum planar cuts to get 64 identical pieces if restacking between cuts is allowed?

hints.1: Think how cuts are split across the three axes, and whether pieces can be stacked.
hints.2: Fixed cuts → maximize (x+1)(y+1)(z+1) with x+y+z fixed; fixed pieces → minimize x+y+z-3; restacking → doubling.

phases.goal: Handle OA wrapping, partial painting, and net-to-cube opposite-face checks.

must_hit.point: OA stories that give large and small edge lengths in physical units require computing n = (large edge)/(small edge) before applying painted-cube formulas.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Extracts n from dimensions first (e.g., 15 cm / 3 cm = 5), then uses the usual counts.

must_hit.point: In a standard cross-shaped net, faces that lie in a straight line and are separated by exactly one face are opposite when folded.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses the alternate-face / skip-one rule on a straight strip of the net.

must_hit.point: In a stair-step (Z-shaped) net, the ends of any Z-shape made of four squares are opposite each other.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Applies the Z-rule to name opposite pairs on a zigzag net.

must_hit.point: A valid folded 3D view never shows two faces that are opposite on the net at the same time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects any view that simultaneously displays a known opposite pair.

probes: A 15 cm cube is painted and cut into 3 cm cubes; what is the probability a random small cube has exactly one face painted?
From a cross-shaped net, which face ends up opposite a given face?
Given opposite pairs from a net, how do you decide which 3D views are valid?

hints.1: Recover n from the story, then fold or paint with the same geometry rules.
hints.2: n = large/small; opposites on a cross skip one square; Z ends of four squares are opposite; visible faces cannot be an opposite pair.
hints.3: 15/3 → n=5 → 6(3)^2=54 of 125; cross skip-one opposites; Z-rule for zigzag nets; drop any view showing both of an opposite pair.

tradeoffs.topic: Even cut split vs close factors
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Fixed cut budget: split cuts across axes as evenly as possible to maximize (x+1)(y+1)(z+1). Fixed piece count on a grid: choose three close factors of the target and use x+y+z-3 cuts.
Without restacking, n×n×n needs 3(n-1) axis-aligned cuts. With restacking, each cut can double pieces, so the theoretical minimum for N pieces is ceil(log2 N) (e.g., 64 → 6).

gotchas.trap: Blindly plugging into 1-face and 2-face formulas when n < 3
gotchas.correction: Those formulas use (n-2) and require n >= 3. For n=2, (n-2)=0: only the 8 corner cubes exist, all with 3 faces painted.

gotchas.trap: Assuming every die has opposite faces summing to 7
gotchas.correction: Use sum-to-7 only for a stated standard die or a single view. With multiple views, deduce opposites from shared-face rotation rules only.

gotchas.trap: Applying painted-cube formulas before recovering n from an OA story with physical sizes
gotchas.correction: First compute n = (large edge)/(small edge), then apply 8, 12(n-2), 6(n-2)^2, and (n-2)^3.
